name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Syntax-check every .cjs / .js
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          for f in **/*.cjs **/*.js; do
            case "$f" in node_modules/*) continue;; esac
            node --check "$f"
          done
      - name: Install (no secrets required)
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund || true
      - name: Test (runs against the zero-dependency echo path)
        run: npm test

  "scripts": {
    "test": "node examples/demo.cjs >/dev/null && echo ok",

    "llm",

  ],

    "node": ">=18"

  "devDependencies": {}
}

⚡ Output Speed

The four $0 levers that make LLM calls faster — emit fewer tokens, route to the fastest capable seat, trim the prompt, and measure tok/s so regressions are numbers, not vibes.
Output Speed encodes a simple truth: LLM wall-clock scales roughly linearly with the tokens you ask a model to emit. So the biggest free speedup is emitting fewer of them. budgetFor(kind) right-sizes max_tokens per task kind (a classification never gets a 4000-token budget; a code file never gets starved below its floor). fastLane(kind) names the fastest seat that is still capable of the kind — mechanical work on a fast low-effort seat, judging on a strong one. trimPrompt() collapses whitespace runs for a faster time-to-first-token without touching content. And record()/report() log tokens-per-second per call to a JSONL ledger, so a speed regression is a measured number you can diff — not a feeling. Zero dependencies, nothing throws.

--- ## Why Output Speed Teams reach for faster hardware and paid fast modes while leaving the free levers on the table. Lever one: output-token reduction — wall-clock tracks the tokens emitted, so right-sized max_tokens per task kind is the single biggest $0 speedup; Output Speed ships sane per-kind budgets with a hard floor so reasoning never gets starved. Lever two: seat routing — a classification or a mechanical rewrite doesn't need your strongest seat; fastLane(kind) maps each kind to the fastest seat that is still capable, and you rename the seats to whatever models you run. Lever three: prompt trim — collapsing trailing whitespace and blank-line runs cuts input tokens and speeds time-to-first-token with zero semantic risk. Lever four — the one that keeps the other three honest: record() stamps every call's tokens/sec into a ledger and report() aggregates by model, so when something gets slower you see it in a number the same day. Raising a budget requires evidence of truncation, not vibes. --- ## What it does | Module | What it does | Signal | |---|---|---| | **budgetFor(kind)** | Right-sized max_tokens per task kind, floored so reasoning is never starved; explicit caller asks are honored above the floor | the biggest $0 speedup | | **fastLane(kind)** | Maps each task kind to the fastest seat still capable of it — seats are names you point at your own models | 3-10x decode on mechanical work | | **trimPrompt()** | Collapses trailing whitespace + blank-line runs — fewer input tokens, faster time-to-first-token, content untouched | free TTFT | | **record() / report()** | Logs tokens/sec per call to data/output-speed.jsonl; aggregates avg tok/s + latency by model over N days | regressions are numbers | --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD T["task (kind, prompt)"] --> B["budgetFor(kind)\nright-sized max_tokens, floored"] T --> L["fastLane(kind)\nfastest capable seat + effort"] T --> P["trimPrompt()\nfewer input tokens → faster TTFT"] B --> C["the LLM call"] L --> C P --> C C --> R["record(label, model, ms, tokens)\n→ data/output-speed.jsonl"] R --> REP["report(days)\navg tok/s + latency by model"] classDef acc fill:#3d3517,stroke:#E0C24C,color:#fff; class B acc; class R acc; ``` --- ## Quickstart ```bash # 1. see the levers work end-to-end (deterministic demo, no API key) node examples/demo.cjs # 2. right-size a call in your own client node -e "const os=require('./lib/output-speed.cjs'); console.log(os.budgetFor('classify'), os.fastLane('classify'))" # 3. record a real call's speed after it returns node -e "require('./lib/output-speed.cjs').record({label:'demo', model:'my-model', ms:1200, out_tokens:480})" # 4. read the scoreboard — avg tok/s + latency per model, last 7 days node lib/output-speed.cjs ``` > Drop the module in front of any LLM client: ask budgetFor(kind) before you set max_tokens, fastLane(kind) before you pick a model, trimPrompt() before you send, and record() after the reply lands. The ledger lives at ./data/output-speed.jsonl (override with OUTPUT_SPEED_LOG). configure({ budgets, lanes }) merges your own kinds and seat names. Nothing here ever throws into your call path. --- ## See it run

--- ## Repository layout ``` output-speed/ ├── lib/ │ └── output-speed.cjs ← budgetFor · fastLane · trimPrompt · record · report · configure ├── examples/ │ └── demo.cjs ← simulates a mixed workload, prints the per-model tok/s scoreboard └── data/ ← output-speed.jsonl ledger (gitignored, auto-created) ``` --- ## Concepts | Concept | Meaning | |---|---| | **Output-token reduction** | Lever #1. Wall-clock scales ~linearly with tokens emitted, so right-sized max_tokens per task kind is the biggest free speedup. | | **Kind budget** | The per-kind answer cap (classify 300, judge 1600, code_file 8000, ...). Raising one requires evidence of truncation, not vibes. | | **Floor** | The hard minimum (256) below which no budget ever drops — speed never comes out of reasoning quality. | | **Seat** | A logical model slot (fast, scout, reader, coder, judge, panel) that you bind to whatever models you actually run. | | **Fast lane** | The fastest seat that is still capable of a task kind — mechanical work decodes 3-10x faster off the strong seat. | | **TTFT** | Time to first token. trimPrompt() cuts input tokens with zero semantic risk, which cuts TTFT for free. | | **tok/s ledger** | record() stamps every call's tokens-per-second into JSONL; report() aggregates by model, so a regression is a diffable number. | --- ## Design principles 1. **The fastest token is the one you don't emit.** Wall-clock scales with output tokens; per-kind budgets are the speed system. 2. **Floors before budgets.** No kind is ever starved below the floor — speed never comes out of reasoning quality. 3. **Route by capability, not habit.** The fastest seat that is still capable wins the kind; strong seats are reserved for judgment. 4. **Measured, not vibed.** Every call can log tok/s; a regression is a diffable number the same day it happens. ---

what it does

Four levers, all free.

01 / BUDGET

Right-size every answer

A classify call gets ~300 tokens, a judge verdict ~1600, a code file 8000 — and nothing ever drops below the floor. Budgets are data, not folklore: raising one requires evidence of truncation in your logs. Callers that explicitly ask for more are honored, floored.

02 / ROUTE

The fastest capable seat

Seats are logical names — fast, scout, reader, coder, judge, panel — that you map to whatever models you actually run. Mechanical and classification work rides the fast seat at low effort; judging stays on a strong seat. configure() merges your own lanes and budgets at runtime.

03 / MEASURE

Vibes don't regress — numbers do

Every call you record() lands as a JSONL line with model, latency, tokens, and computed tok/s — measured token counts preferred, chars/4 as the honest fallback. report(days) rolls it up per model, so the day a provider gets slower, your ledger says so.

quickstart

Up and running in a clone.

Every value comes from .env. Nothing here is tied to any account — bring your own.

# 1. see the levers work end-to-end (deterministic demo, no API key)
node examples/demo.cjs

# 2. right-size a call in your own client
node -e "const os=require('./lib/output-speed.cjs'); console.log(os.budgetFor('classify'), os.fastLane('classify'))"

# 3. record a real call's speed after it returns
node -e "require('./lib/output-speed.cjs').record({label:'demo', model:'my-model', ms:1200, out_tokens:480})"

# 4. read the scoreboard — avg tok/s + latency per model, last 7 days
node lib/output-speed.cjs

# Output Speed — Architecture

Output Speed encodes a simple truth: LLM wall-clock scales roughly linearly with the tokens you ask a model to emit. So the biggest free speedup is emitting fewer of them. budgetFor(kind) right-sizes max_tokens per task kind (a classification never gets a 4000-token budget; a code file never gets starved below its floor). fastLane(kind) names the fastest seat that is still capable of the kind — mechanical work on a fast low-effort seat, judging on a strong one. trimPrompt() collapses whitespace runs for a faster time-to-first-token without touching content. And record()/report() log tokens-per-second per call to a JSONL ledger, so a speed regression is a measured number you can diff — not a feeling. Zero dependencies, nothing throws.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    T["task (kind, prompt)"] --> B["budgetFor(kind)\nright-sized max_tokens, floored"]
    T --> L["fastLane(kind)\nfastest capable seat + effort"]
    T --> P["trimPrompt()\nfewer input tokens → faster TTFT"]
    B --> C["the LLM call"]
    L --> C
    P --> C
    C --> R["record(label, model, ms, tokens)\n→ data/output-speed.jsonl"]
    R --> REP["report(days)\navg tok/s + latency by model"]
    classDef acc fill:#3d3517,stroke:#E0C24C,color:#fff;
    class B acc;
    class R acc;
```

## How it fits together

Output Speed is a single pure-Node module with two tables and four functions. KIND_BUDGETS maps task kinds (classify, short_reply, mechanical, email_draft, judge, code_patch, code_file, ...) to right-sized max_tokens caps; budgetFor(kind, requested) returns the explicit caller request when given (floored at FLOOR=256) or the kind budget otherwise, so no call is ever starved below the floor and no classification ever burns a code-file budget. LANES maps kinds to { seat, effort } pairs where seats are logical names — fast, scout, reader, coder, judge, panel — that the host application binds to real models; fastLane(kind) is a lookup with a default, and configure({ budgets, lanes }) shallow-merges caller overrides so an application can rename seats or retune budgets at runtime without forking the table. trimPrompt(s) strips trailing whitespace per line and collapses 3+ blank lines to one — a semantics-free input-token cut that speeds time-to-first-token. record({ label, model, ms, text | out_tokens }) computes tokens/sec (measured out_tokens preferred, chars/4 fallback), appends one JSONL line to the ledger (OUTPUT_SPEED_LOG or ./data/output-speed.jsonl), and returns the tps — wrapped so it never throws into the caller's request path. report(days) scans the ledger once and aggregates count, avg tok/s, and avg latency per model over the window. The CLI prints the 7-day scoreboard.

## Extending it

Every capability is a self-contained module. To add your own, follow the contract the existing
modules use and wire it into the entry point. Keep it portable — config via `.env`, no hardcoded
paths, no personal accounts.

## Design principles

1. **The fastest token is the one you don't emit.** Wall-clock scales with output tokens; per-kind budgets are the speed system.
2. **Floors before budgets.** No kind is ever starved below the floor — speed never comes out of reasoning quality.
3. **Route by capability, not habit.** The fastest seat that is still capable wins the kind; strong seats are reserved for judgment.
4. **Measured, not vibed.** Every call can log tok/s; a regression is a diffable number the same day it happens.
